security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by markdown fences, inline code, and visible bash examples in SKILL.md. The skill shows legitimate GitHub project-management intent, but it carries medium contextual risk from unpinned third-party npx commands, automated GitHub mutations, and external webhook sync.

remediation.suggestion: Pin stable versions of ruv-swarm and claude-flow, document package verification steps, and prefer audited local installs for repeated use.
Add dry-run mode, explicit user confirmation, and clear rollback guidance before close, archive, bulk move, or recovery workflows.
Require trusted HTTPS endpoints, request signing, authentication, minimal payloads, and documentation for private repository data handling.
Validate issue numbers, project identifiers, labels, and repository names before passing them to shell commands or GitHub CLI operations.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Third-Party CLI Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells users to run npx claude-flow@alpha and many npx ruv-swarm commands. These commands execute third-party package code in a repository context without pinning a stable version or documenting an integrity check.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The npx commands are explicit and frequent, and they would run external package code if executed. No hidden malware intent was found, so the severity is medium rather than high.

semantic_findings.title: Automated GitHub State Changes Without Confirmation Gates
semantic_findings.description: Several workflows can close duplicate or stale issues, auto-move project cards, and archive completed board items. These are legitimate project operations, but they can cause unwanted repository state changes without a required dry run or approval step.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines directly show close, auto-management, and archive behavior. The risk is business-logic impact from documented automation, not covert destructive behavior.

semantic_findings.title: External Webhook Sync May Expose Project Metadata
semantic_findings.description: The real-time board sync example sends updates to an external webhook endpoint. If users configure an untrusted endpoint, private issue, board, or milestone metadata could leave the repository boundary.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The webhook is a placeholder and the skill mentions webhook security, but the workflow still encourages external sync. The data exposure depends on the endpoint a user configures.

content.user_title: Manage GitHub Projects with Swarm Workflows
content.value_statement: GitHub projects can drift across issues, boards, milestones, and sprint rituals. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured workflows for coordinated GitHub planning and automation.
actual_capabilities: Creates and triages GitHub issues using GitHub CLI and MCP workflow examples.
Converts GitHub issues into swarm tasks, subtasks, labels, and progress updates.
Initializes and synchronizes GitHub Projects boards with status fields and views.
Plans sprints, milestones, release coordination, and cross-repository work.
Generates board analytics, KPI reports, standup summaries, and progress tracking workflows.
Provides reusable issue templates and GitHub Actions workflow examples.
limitations: Requires authenticated GitHub CLI access and repository or project permissions.
Many workflows depend on ruv-swarm or claude-flow being installed and trusted.
Automation can change issues and boards, so commands need review before use.
Does not replace GitHub access controls, package verification, or webhook security.

use_cases.title: Triage a Busy Issue Backlog
use_cases.description: Group unlabeled issues by priority, assign labels, identify duplicates, and prepare coordinated follow-up work.

use_cases.title: Run a Sprint Planning Board
use_cases.description: Create board fields, sprint views, milestone tracking, and progress reporting for an upcoming development cycle.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Multi-Repository Delivery
use_cases.description: Track dependencies, release milestones, and work distribution across related repositories and project boards.

prompt_templates.title: Start Issue Triage
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the GitHub project management skill to create a clear issue triage plan for this repository. Include labels, priorities, owners, and next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan One Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to turn issue number 123 into a coordinated implementation plan. Break it into subtasks, owners, review points, and progress updates.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Sprint Board
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a GitHub Projects board workflow for the next sprint. Include fields, columns, automation rules, and review gates.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate a Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to coordinate a cross-repository release plan. Include milestone tracking, dependency handling, risk controls, and reporting checkpoints.

output_examples.input: Triage unlabeled GitHub issues before sprint planning.
output: Issues are grouped into bug, enhancement, documentation, and investigation queues.
Each queue includes suggested labels, priority levels, and recommended owners.
Duplicate candidates and blocked items are called out for manual review.

output_examples.input: Create a sprint board workflow for a feature team.
output: The board includes Backlog, Ready, In Progress, Review, Blocked, and Done states.
Custom fields track priority, swarm status, owner, milestone, and target sprint.
Review gates require manual approval before automated status changes.

output_examples.input: Prepare a release coordination plan across several repositories.
output: The plan lists release milestones, dependency risks, cross-repository owners, and reporting cadence.
It defines escalation points for blocked issues and late testing feedback.
It recommends final verification before project board automation changes shared state.

best_practices: Confirm the repository, project board, labels, and permissions before running automation.
Use dry-run review or manual approval before closing, archiving, or bulk-moving work.
Pin and verify third-party CLI packages before using npx-based workflows.
anti_patterns: Running automated close or archive commands on production repositories without review.
Sending project sync data to unverified webhook endpoints.
Granting broad GitHub permissions when narrower scopes are enough.

faq.question: Does this skill require GitHub CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented shell workflows assume GitHub CLI is installed, authenticated, and authorized for the target repository.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code, with workflows written as reusable prompts and command examples.

faq.question: Will it change my GitHub repository automatically?
faq.answer: Some examples create, edit, close, or move GitHub issues and project items. Review commands before execution.

faq.question: Does it manage private repository data?
faq.answer: It can read and process issue, project, milestone, and board data when permissions allow it. Use least-privilege access.

faq.question: Are the swarm tools built into GitHub?
faq.answer: No. The workflows reference external tools such as ruv-swarm and claude-flow that must be installed and trusted separately.

faq.question: What should I verify before using webhook sync?
faq.answer: Verify the endpoint owner, authentication, signing, data scope, and retention policy before sending project updates.
